messages:
Dylan Brooks: final pre-beta checklist for Shadow Evals / shadow traffic. can folks sanity-check we’re green on: kill switch, safe defaults, dashboards/alerts, and capacity budgets?

Paula Mendes: +1. need explicit “default OFF unless allowlisted” callout for release notes + internal comms.

Benji Okafor: policy side: RoutePolicy `shadow_traffic` field merged (PR-48244). migration sets null => treated as disabled. we also block config if sampling_pct > 0 AND no allowlist present.

Jordan Lee: adding: validation also forces `shadow_targets` non-empty if sampling_pct > 0. and max sampling_pct capped per tier (from Cole’s quota service).

Cole Summers: quotas/budgets: global cap enforced at runtime + queue admission.
- default sampling_pct = 0
- per-route max (beta): 0.5% (hosted), 0.2% (dedicated) unless override
- per-customer shadow token budget is separate meter; goes hard-deny when exceeded (no spill into primary)

Sean Gallagher: SRE checklist items:
- kill switch verified works without deploy ✅
- queue depth alerts in place ✅
- drop counters dashboarded ✅
- runbook linked from oncall hub ✅
Primary-path p99 budget: perf canary is clean.

Allison Grant: dashboards: Grafana panels landed (observability-pack PR-287) + wired into SRE overview. also the shadow_eval.* metrics naming matches the tagging spec, and Thomas’ allowlist is on.

Thomas Baird: cardinality guardrails are enabled in staging + canary. tags limited to:
- route_id (hashed)
- primary_model_id (bucketed)
- shadow_target_id (bucketed)
- region
- outcome
No raw customer_id, no prompt_id. Anything else gets dropped + increments `shadow_eval.tag_dropped_count`.

Marissa Cole: Console: the Shadow Evals dashboard is behind beta flag. data shows up for the test accounts. copy is explicit: “does not affect user responses; shadow requests may be dropped under load.”

Chloe Martin: +1. backend query endpoints have permission checks (route-level). also pagination caps so nobody tries to pull raw events.

Rafael Mendes: re kill switch: I ran the runbook steps this morning on staging.
- toggled global kill switch -> queue stops accepting new shadow jobs immediately
- in-flight shadows allowed to finish (bounded)
- verified `shadow_eval.shadow_drop_count` spikes as expected
Runbook: /confluence/runbook-shadow-runner-kill-switch

Benji Okafor: can we confirm semantics: kill switch is “deny admission” not “force-cancel in-flight”? want to ensure we don’t introduce weird worker cancels.

Sean Gallagher: yep. admission-only. if we need hard cancel we’d have to deploy a worker change; not doing that for beta.

Keiko Yamamoto: autoscaling/guardrails: shadow runner has its own pool + separate HPA. hard ceiling is set per region. if it hits ceiling, admission control drops shadows (does not backpressure gateway).

Mina Haddad: routing note: shadow targets resolved from policy snapshot at request time; shadow uses same request_id + trace id propagation. if policy can’t resolve target, shadow is skipped and counted.

Dylan Brooks: any remaining “gotchas” before we call go?

Thomas Baird: one thing: ensure we keep `shadow_target_id` bucketing stable across deploys. today it’s hashed by (model+version+quant_profile). good.

Allison Grant: also ensured retention defaults are the “metrics only” path. raw payload logging remains off by default and requires restricted access flag.

Paula Mendes: product checklist: beta scope explicitly excludes customer-configurable judge prompts (we ship templates only). gating in rollouts references aggregated metrics only (win-rate, format adherence, latency delta). no per-request debugging in beta.

Marissa Cole: comms ready. beta enablement doc points customers to “Shadow Evals” and the quota language.

Rafael Mendes: can we confirm alert thresholds?

Sean Gallagher: current paging:
- queue_depth > 50k for 10m (page)
- shadow_error_rate > 5% for 15m (ticket)
- shadow_drop_rate > 20% for 15m (ticket)
No alerts tied to primary SLOs (separate). If primary p99 moves, incident is the primary system, shadow is first suspect and we flip kill switch.

DeployBot: Deploy scheduled: shadow-runner canary -> prod-us-east at 18:30 PT. Owners: @Sean Gallagher @Dylan Brooks

Jordan Lee: policy rollout sequence confirmed: feature flag stays off in all regions until we explicitly enable per allowlisted account.

Cole Summers: +1 and quotas are already provisioned for the 3 beta accounts (limited) only.

Dylan Brooks: ok, sounds like go. action items before tomorrow:
- Sean/Rafa: double-check kill switch perms for oncall role
- Marissa/Paula: finalize beta enablement email + “default off” wording
- Thomas/Allison: final review of tag allowlist is on in prod config

Marissa Cole: ack. (reactions: :thumbsup: x4)

Sean Gallagher: ack. (reactions: :white_check_mark: x3)

Thomas Baird: ack. (reactions: :thumbsup: x2)
